chapter: Arriving in New York: the Nest Club and Harlem nightlife
title: Bill Bottoms of the Royal Garden and King Jones, the first MC
summary: Danny recalls the Chicago manager Bill Bottoms and MC King Jones, who introduced King Oliver and Freddie Keppard as two kings on one throne.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: You've got to live up to it!
You had Bill Bottoms. All them kind of names. Bill Bottoms...
That was a Chicago cat. He had a cabaret out in...
What was the name of that (?) in Chicago?
Yeah, but he owned the Royal...not the Royal Garden... Yeah, the Royal Garden.
Yeah, Bill Bottoms was the manager of the Royal Garden. And that little-bitty guy, what's his name...Jones -- King Jones. "La-deez on gentlemen!" You know Little King Jones, the MC?

King Jones used to announce King Oliver and Freddie Keppard, who at one period they both played in the band together. He said, "Two kings on one throne. First time you ever seen that, la-deez on..." Paul used to laugh. He said, "La-deez on gentleman." And these ladies were sitting on (?), grabbing his head. He used to do that every night. Yeah, I saw him. And later on, he was around the Savoy; he had Something with King Jones.
Yeah, King Jones was the first MC. As Paul said, he was the MC that they had that would out on the stage and announce with emphasis. Well, I had the pleasure of meeting him, you know.
